project.title: Instagram - Photo Sharing Platform
project.description: A comprehensive system design for a scalable photo-sharing platform supporting billions of users with features like photo/video upload, feed generation, likes, comments, stories, and real-time notifications.

functional.title: Photo/Video Upload
functional.description: Users can upload photos and videos with captions, filters, and location tags

functional.title: Personalized Feed
functional.description: Users see a ranked feed of posts from people they follow
acceptanceCriteria: Feed ordered by relevance (not just chronological)

functional.title: Social Interactions
functional.description: Users can like, comment, and share posts

functional.title: Follow/Unfollow Users
functional.description: Users can follow and unfollow other users to curate their feed

functional.title: Stories (24h ephemeral content)
functional.description: Users can post photos/videos that disappear after 24 hours

nonFunctional.title: Scale
nonFunctional.description: Support 2 billion+ monthly active users, 100M+ daily photo uploads

nonFunctional.title: Low Latency
nonFunctional.description: Feed loads in under 1 second, image previews in under 200ms

nonFunctional.title: Eventual Consistency
nonFunctional.description: Like counts and follower counts can be eventually consistent
acceptanceCriteria: Feed can show slightly stale data (5-10s lag acceptable)

assumptions: Users primarily consume content (90% viewers, 10% creators)
constraints: Must comply with GDPR and data privacy laws
Content moderation required for harmful content
Minimize storage costs while maintaining quality
Support offline viewing of cached content

calculations.title: Photo Storage Requirements
calculations.formula: Daily uploads × Average size × Redundancy × Retention

calculations.title: Bandwidth Requirements
calculations.formula: Daily reads × Average image size / 86400 seconds

calculations.title: Cache Memory Requirements
calculations.formula: Hot users × Feed size × Metadata size

assumptions: 80% of traffic goes to 20% of content (hot content)
Cache hit rate of 85% for feed generation
references: Instagram Engineering Blog - Scaling to billions
Industry benchmarks for social media platforms

content.markdown:
# Instagram System Architecture

Instagram's architecture is designed to handle **billions of users**, **100M+ daily photo uploads**, and **500M+ daily stories** with low latency and high availability.

## System Layers

### 1. Client Layer
- **CDN (CloudFront/Cloudflare)**: Globally distributed edge servers for serving images and videos with <200ms latency
- Mobile apps (iOS/Android) and web clients

### 2. Gateway Layer
- **Load Balancer (NGINX/AWS ALB)**: Distributes incoming traffic across API servers
- Health checks and automatic failover

### 3. Application Layer
- **API Servers**: Stateless REST/GraphQL servers (Python/Django, Node.js, Go)
- **Feed Generation Service**: Personalized feed ranking using ML (TensorFlow, Redis)
- **Media Upload Service**: Photo/video processing (Go, FFmpeg, ImageMagick)
- **Notification Service**: Real-time push notifications (WebSockets, Firebase)
- **Search Service**: User/hashtag/location search (Elasticsearch)

### 4. Data Layer
- **PostgreSQL**: User profiles, post metadata, relationships (sharded by user_id)
- **Cassandra**: User timelines and activity feeds (fan-out on write)
- **Redis**: Hot data caching (feed cache, session data)
- **S3**: Raw photo/video storage with multi-region replication

### 5. Messaging Layer
- **Kafka**: Event streaming for feed updates, notifications, analytics
- Async processing and data pipelines

### 6. ML Layer
- **ML Pipeline**: Content recommendation, spam detection, moderation (TensorFlow, PyTorch)

## Key Data Flows

### Photo Upload Flow
1. User uploads photo → API Server
2. API Server → Media Upload Service (resize, compress)
3. Upload Service → S3 (store raw + thumbnails)
4. Upload Service → PostgreSQL (save metadata)
5. Publish event → Kafka
6. Kafka → Feed Service (fan-out to followers)
7. Feed Service → Cassandra (update follower feeds)

### Feed Generation Flow
1. User requests feed → API Server
2. API Server → Feed Service
3. Feed Service → Redis (check cache)
4. If cache miss → Cassandra (fetch timeline)
5. Feed Service → ML Pipeline (rank posts)
6. Return ranked feed → Client

## Technology Stack

**Frontend**: React Native, Swift, Kotlin, PWA

**Backend**: Python/Django, Node.js, Go, GraphQL

**Databases**: PostgreSQL (sharded), Cassandra, Redis Cluster

**Storage**: AWS S3, CloudFront CDN

**Messaging**: Apache Kafka, RabbitMQ

**Infrastructure**: AWS, Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform

**ML/Search**: TensorFlow, Elasticsearch, Apache Spark

# Component Deep Dive

## Infrastructure Components

### CDN (CloudFront/Cloudflare)
- **Purpose**: Globally distributed edge caching for images/videos
- **Technologies**: CloudFront, Cloudflare, Akamai
- **Benefits**:
  - <200ms image load times worldwide
  - 90% reduction in origin server load
  - Automatic DDoS protection

### Load Balancer (NGINX/AWS ALB)
- **Purpose**: Distribute traffic across API servers
- **Technologies**: NGINX, AWS ALB, HAProxy
- **Features**:
  - Layer 7 (HTTP) and Layer 4 (TCP) load balancing
  - Health checks every 10 seconds
  - Auto-scaling integration

## Application Components

### API Servers
- **Purpose**: Handle all user requests (REST/GraphQL)
- **Technologies**: Python/Django, Node.js, Go
- **Scale**: 1000+ servers, auto-scale based on CPU >70%

### Feed Generation Service
- **Purpose**: Create personalized user feeds
- **Technologies**: Python, TensorFlow, Redis
- **Approach**: Hybrid fan-out (write for regular users, read for celebrities)
- **Ranking**: ML model predicting engagement probability

### Media Upload Service
- **Purpose**: Process photo/video uploads
- **Technologies**: Go, FFmpeg, ImageMagick
- **Processing**:
  - Resize to 3 sizes (thumbnail 150px, medium 640px, full 1080px)
  - Convert to WebP (30% size reduction) with JPEG fallback
  - Async processing (returns 202 Accepted immediately)

### Notification Service
- **Purpose**: Real-time push notifications
- **Technologies**: WebSockets, Firebase, APNS/FCM
- **Scale**: 10M+ concurrent WebSocket connections

### Search Service
- **Purpose**: User/hashtag/location search
- **Technologies**: Elasticsearch, Solr
- **Indexing**: Near real-time (5-second lag)

## Data Components

### PostgreSQL (User/Post Metadata)
- **Purpose**: ACID transactions for critical data
- **Sharding**: 256 shards by user_id (consistent hashing)
- **Replication**: 1 master + 2 read replicas per shard
- **Scale**: ~8M users per shard at 2B scale

### Cassandra (Activity Feeds)
- **Purpose**: Write-heavy timeline storage
- **Partition Key**: user_id
- **Clustering Key**: post_timestamp (DESC)
- **Replication Factor**: 3
- **Consistency**: QUORUM (2/3)

### Redis (Cache)
- **Purpose**: Hot data caching
- **Structure**:
  - feed:{user_id} → List of top 100 post IDs
  - post:{post_id} → Post metadata JSON
  - user:{user_id} → User profile JSON
- **Eviction**: LRU for memory management
- **TTL**: 5-30 minutes depending on data type

### S3 (Object Storage)
- **Purpose**: Raw photo/video storage
- **Replication**: 3x cross-region
- **Cost**: ~$10K/day for 100M daily uploads
- **Lifecycle**: Archive to Glacier after 1 year

## Messaging Components

### Kafka (Event Streaming)
- **Purpose**: Async event processing
- **Topics**:
  - post_created → Feed fan-out
  - user_action → Analytics
  - notification → Push notifications
- **Retention**: 7 days
- **Partitions**: 100+ for parallelism

## ML Components

### ML Pipeline
- **Purpose**: Recommendation, moderation, spam detection
- **Technologies**: TensorFlow, PyTorch, Apache Spark
- **Models**:
  - Feed ranking (engagement prediction)
  - Content moderation (NSFW detection)
  - Spam detection (fake accounts, bot behavior)

examples.title: Users Table (PostgreSQL)
examples.code:
CREATE TABLE users (
  user_id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  username VARCHAR(30) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  password_hash VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  full_name VARCHAR(100),
  bio TEXT,
  profile_image_url VARCHAR(500),
  is_verified BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
  is_private BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
  
  -- Counters (updated asynchronously)
  follower_count INT DEFAULT 0,
  following_count INT DEFAULT 0,
  post_count INT DEFAULT 0
);

CREATE INDEX idx_users_username ON users(username);
CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users(email);

examples.title: Posts Table (PostgreSQL)
examples.code:
CREATE TABLE posts (
  post_id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(user_id),
  media_url VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL,
  media_type VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, -- 'photo' or 'video'
  caption TEXT,
  location VARCHAR(200),
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
  
  -- Denormalized counters (updated async via Kafka)
  like_count INT DEFAULT 0,
  comment_count INT DEFAULT 0,
  share_count INT DEFAULT 0,
  
  -- Soft delete
  is_deleted BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE
);

CREATE INDEX idx_posts_user_id ON posts(user_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_posts_created_at ON posts(created_at DESC);

pages.title: Deep Dive: Feed Generation
pages.description: Detailed analysis of feed ranking algorithm

content.markdown:
# Feed Generation Strategy

## Fan-out Approach: Hybrid (Fan-out on Write + Fan-out on Read)

### Why Hybrid?
- **Celebrity users** (millions of followers): Fan-out on read (on-demand)
- **Regular users** (<1000 followers): Fan-out on write (pre-computed)
- **Threshold**: 10,000 followers

### Fan-out on Write (Regular Users)

**When a user posts:**
1. Post saved to `posts` table
2. Fetch follower list from `follows` table
3. For each follower, insert into their `user_feed` (Cassandra)
4. Publish event to Kafka for async processing

**Pros:**
- Fast feed reads (pre-computed)
- Simple implementation

**Cons:**
- Slow writes for users with many followers
- Wasted storage if follower doesn't check feed

### Fan-out on Read (Celebrity Users)

**When user requests feed:**
1. Fetch list of followees
2. Identify celebrity followees (>10K followers)
3. Fetch recent posts from celebrities on-demand
4. Merge with pre-computed feed from regular users
5. Rank by ML model

**Pros:**
- Scales for celebrity users
- No wasted storage

**Cons:**
- Slower feed generation
- More complex implementation

## Ranking Algorithm

**Factors:**
- **Recency**: Newer posts ranked higher (decay function)
- **Engagement**: Like/comment count weighted by recency
- **User affinity**: How often user interacts with author
- **Content type**: Photos vs videos (user preference)
- **Completion rate**: Video watch time

**ML Model:**
- Logistic regression predicting "probability user will engage"
- Features: user-author relationship, post engagement, time since post
- Trained on historical engagement data
- Served via TensorFlow Serving

# Scalability Strategies

## Database Sharding

### PostgreSQL Sharding (Users & Posts)

**Sharding Key**: `user_id` (consistent hashing)

**Why user_id?**
- Most queries filtered by user_id
- Avoids cross-shard joins
- Even distribution

**Shard Count**: 256 shards (2^8)
- Allows splitting shards as we grow
- Each shard handles ~8M users at 2B scale

## Caching Strategy

### Redis Cluster

**Cache Structure:**
```
feed:{user_id} → List of post_ids (top 100)
post:{post_id} → Post metadata JSON
user:{user_id} → User profile JSON
like_count:{post_id} → Counter
```

**Cache Invalidation:**
- **Write-through**: Update cache on write
- **TTL-based**: Expire stale data (5-30 min)
- **Event-driven**: Kafka events trigger invalidation

## CDN for Media

### Image Serving Pipeline

1. **Upload**: User → S3 (origin)
2. **Processing**: Lambda resize (3 sizes: thumb, medium, full)
3. **CDN**: CloudFront edge caching
4. **Delivery**: User requests from nearest edge

**Image Formats:**
- WebP for modern browsers (30% smaller)
- JPEG fallback for compatibility
- Automatic format detection via `Accept` header

# Reliability & Fault Tolerance

## Multi-Region Deployment

**Active-Active Architecture:**
- 3 regions: US-East, US-West, EU-West
- Each region fully independent
- Cross-region replication (async)

**Benefits:**
- Low latency (route to nearest region)
- Regional failover in <1 minute
- Survive entire region outage

items.title: Eventual Consistency for Like Counts
items.description: Accept slightly stale like counts (5-10s lag) in exchange for higher write throughput. Use counter cache updated asynchronously.

items.title: Pre-compute Feeds (Fan-out on Write)
items.description: Store duplicate feed data in Cassandra for fast reads, accepting higher storage cost (~50TB for 500M users).

items.title: CDN Costs vs Latency
items.description: Pay for global CDN (~$10K/day) to achieve <200ms image loads worldwide. Alternative: Single-region storage would save 80% cost but increase latency 10x.

items.title: PostgreSQL for User/Post Metadata
items.description: Use RDBMS for structured data needing ACID guarantees (follows, user profiles). Accept sharding complexity. Alternative: NoSQL (DynamoDB) simpler but loses transactions.

items.title: Cassandra for Activity Feeds
items.description: Use wide-column store for write-heavy timeline data. Accept eventual consistency. Alternative: Redis (faster reads) but limited by memory cost.

items.title: ML-based Feed Ranking
items.description: Invest in ML infrastructure for personalized feeds (higher engagement). Accept complexity and operational cost. Alternative: Chronological feed (simpler but lower retention).
